title: Weyl alternant identity for split characteristic-zero group representations
statement:
Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine semisimple simply connected group scheme over $\mathbf Q$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Semisimple means that after algebraic closure there is no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup; solvable means that iterated commutator subgroups vanish. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism from a connected semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a split maximal torus, isomorphic to a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$ and maximal after algebraic closure. Write $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf G_m,T)$ for the finite-rank free character and cocharacter lattices, paired perfectly by $\chi\circ\eta:t\mapsto t^{\langle\chi,\eta\rangle}$. Let $\Phi\subset X$ and $\alpha^\vee\in Y$ be the roots and coroots of $(G,T)$: the roots are the nonzero $T$-weights of the adjoint action on the identity tangent Lie algebra, and a coroot is normalized by the opposite root subgroups, with $\langle\alpha,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2$. Suppose they form a spanning finite reduced crystallographic root datum: the root and dual reflections permute the root-coroot pairs, proportional roots differ only by sign, and their reflection group $W$ is finite. Fix a simple-root base $\Delta$ and its positive roots $\Phi^+$, so the simple roots are linearly independent and every root has integer simple coordinates all nonnegative or all nonpositive. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$ in $X\otimes\mathbf Q$.

Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional simple algebraic-group representation [def-wf-algebraic-representations]: its only subspaces invariant after every scalar extension are $0,V$. Suppose $\lambda\in X$ is dominant, $\langle\lambda,\delta^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for $\delta\in\Delta$, and that there is $v\ne0$ on which $T$ acts by $\lambda$ and every positive-root Lie subspace acts by zero in the differentiated representation. Lie algebras and differentiation here mean the identity tangent spaces, or infinitesimal points over $\mathbf Q[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$; the action is a Lie representation [def-wf-lie-algebra]. For $\chi\in X$ let $V_\chi$ be its $T$-weight space. Then $V=\bigoplus_{\chi\in X}V_\chi$ with only finitely many nonzero summands, $\rho\in X$, and in the group algebra $\mathbf Q[X]$, with $e^\xi e^\eta=e^{\xi+\eta}$, one has
$$q\,A(\rho)=A(\lambda+\rho),\qquad q=\sum_{\chi\in X}(\dim_{\mathbf Q}V_\chi)e^\chi,\qquad A(\nu)=\sum_{w\in W}\det(w)e^{w\nu}.$$
Here the determinant is on $X\otimes\mathbf Q$. This is a polynomial identity and does not mean evaluation of a fraction with zero denominator. It includes reducible and empty root systems.

proof.text: Restrict $V$ to the specified split torus. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition], $V=\bigoplus_\chi V_\chi$ with finite support. Choose an algebraic closure $F$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-geometric-root-comparison] to obtain $S=G_F$, $T_F$, the same lattices, root datum and chosen positive system, and a Borel $B$ with $U=R_u(B)$. By [lem-sfb-split-simple-absolute-irreducibility], $V_F=F\otimes_{\mathbf Q}V$ is simple. The tensor products of bases of the $V_\chi$ form a basis of $V_F$, on which $T_F$ has the same diagonal characters. Thus $(V_F)_\chi=F\otimes V_\chi$ and $\dim_F(V_F)_\chi=\dim_{\mathbf Q}V_\chi$: comparing coordinates in that basis proves equality, since distinct characters remain distinct under the cited lattice bijection. In particular its formal character is the same integer sum $q$. Differentiating the scalar-extended action over dual numbers extends its matrices linearly from $\mathbf Q$ to $F$; the cited root-space tangent comparison therefore shows that $v_F=1\otimes v\ne0$ is still killed by all positive-root Lie spaces and has weight $\lambda$.

source.place: 22a, printed p.463; 22.4, printed p.464; the scalar comparison is by the displayed weight basis and tangent functor.

proof.text: The group $S$ is semisimple and hence reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. By [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules], the half sum of the positive roots belongs to $X^*(T_F)$. The lattice bijection of step 1 identifies its rational half sum with the original $\rho$, hence $\rho\in X$. By [lem-sfb-weyl-reflection-realization], the geometric normalizer Weyl group is exactly the reflection group $W$ in the item. By [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit] it has $w_0^2=1$, $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$ and $w_0\rho=-\rho$. The direct sum for $\operatorname{Lie}(U)$ in step 1 kills $v_F$. Apply [lem-sfb-char-zero-differentiation-hom] to the smooth connected affine group $U$ and the linear map $F\to V_F$, $1\mapsto v_F$, with trivial source action. Its Lie-equivariance is exactly this vanishing, so the map is $U$-equivariant. Thus $U$ fixes $v_F$ after every algebra extension; since $T_F$ acts by $\lambda$ and $B=U\rtimes T_F$, it spans a $B$-eigenline of character $\lambda$. The unique $U$-fixed line in [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight] now identifies the highest weight of $V_F$ as precisely $\lambda$.

source.place: 22.18--22.19, printed pp.467--468; 10.31, printed p.196; actual rho character before 22.50, printed p.480; 22.53, printed p.481.

proof.text: Put $\mu=-w_0\lambda$. By [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight], $V_F^\vee$ is simple and has a nonzero $U$-fixed $T_F$-eigenvector $\ell$ of weight $\mu$. Since $B=U\rtimes T_F$, it is a $B$-eigenvector, and simplicity says it generates $V_F^\vee$. Apply [lem-sfb-primitive-cyclic-weight-bound]: every weight $\eta$ in the dual satisfies $\mu-\eta\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}\Delta$. For a simple root $\delta$, choose a normalizer representative $n$ of $s_\delta$ using the reflection realization in step 2. The vector $n\ell\ne0$ has weight $s_\delta\mu$, since $t(n\ell)=n(n^{-1}tn)\ell=(s_\delta\mu)(t)n\ell$ on every algebra. Consequently $\mu-s_\delta\mu=\langle\mu,\delta^\vee\rangle\delta$ has nonnegative simple-root coordinates. Linear independence of $\Delta$ gives $\langle\mu,\delta^\vee\rangle\ge0$. Thus $\mu$ is dominant. Extend it to $B$ via the projection to $T_F$.

source.place: Contragredient highest weight after 22.31, printed p.471; dominance argument of Proposition 22.17 using normalizer transport 22.15, printed pp.466--467.

proof.text: Write $M_\mu=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\mu}$ on $Q=S/B$. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], its sections are $E(-\mu)=\{f\in F[S]:f(gb)=\mu(b)f(g)\}$, with left translation. Define $j:V_F\to E(-\mu)$ by $j(x)(g)=\ell(g^{-1}x)$. These are regular matrix coefficients, since the representation and inversion are morphisms. The dual eigenvector identity $b\ell=\mu(b)\ell$ means $\ell(b^{-1}y)=\mu(b)\ell(y)$, so $j(x)(gb)=\mu(b)j(x)(g)$. Also $j(sx)(g)=j(x)(s^{-1}g)$, proving equivariance after every algebra extension. Some $x$ has $\ell(x)\ne0$, so evaluation at $1$ shows $j\ne0$. Its kernel is invariant, hence simplicity makes $j$ injective. By [lem-sfb-flag-line-euler-alternant], $H^0(Q,M_\mu)$ is finite dimensional. The homogeneous-section identification supplies its rational $S$-action. By [lem-sfb-characteristic-zero-complete-reducibility], it is a finite sum of simple modules. Each nonzero simple summand contributes a nonzero $U$-fixed line by [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight]. But [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line] says that the entire nonzero $E(-\mu)$ has a one-dimensional $U$-fixed space. There is therefore exactly one simple summand. The nonzero equivariant injection $j$ is consequently an isomorphism $V_F\simeq H^0(Q,M_\mu)$.

source.place: 22.21--22.22, printed pp.468--469; 22.41, printed p.477; 22.48 and the characteristic-zero paragraph following it, printed p.479. Matrix-coefficient realization written explicitly.

proof.text: For $\eta\in X$ write $M_\eta=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\eta}$. Pull back along the faithfully flat right $B$-torsor $S\to Q$ of step 2. The quotient trivializations of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections] identify these pullbacks with trivial lines. Multiplication $(z,z')\mapsto zz'$ commutes with descent data because $\eta(b)\xi(b)=(\eta+\xi)(b)$. By the full faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], it descends to $M_\eta\otimes M_\xi\simeq M_{\eta+\xi}$, with inverse the usual inverse of the multiplication identification of two trivial lines after pullback. The character $0$ has trivial descent data, giving $M_0=\mathcal O_Q$; hence $M_\eta^{-1}=M_{-\eta}$.

source.place: 18c, printed pp.389--390, character descent data and their multiplication.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit], $\langle\rho,\delta^\vee\rangle=1$ for each simple root. Thus the dominance in step 3 makes $\mu+2\rho$ strictly dominant. Apply [lem-sfb-strict-dominant-flag-line-ample]: $Q$ is smooth projective geometrically integral and $M_{\mu+2\rho}$ is ample. By [lem-sfb-flag-canonical-character], $Q$ has pure dimension $|\Phi^+|$ and $\omega_Q\simeq M_{-2\rho}$. Step 5 identifies $\omega_Q\otimes M_{\mu+2\rho}$ with $M_\mu$. All the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-kodaira-vanishing] hold over the algebraically closed characteristic-zero field $F$, so $H^i(Q,M_\mu)=0$ for $i>0$. This uses only the characteristic-zero Kodaira branch, before any positive-characteristic dimension comparison.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-flag-line-euler-alternant] to the character $\mu$. By steps 4 and 6 its Euler character is $q$, so its polynomial identity reads $qA(-ho)=A(-\mu-ho)$. As $\mu=-w_0\lambda$ and $w_0ho=-ho$, the right side is $A(w_0(\lambda+ho))$. Reindexing the defining finite sum by $u=ww_0$ gives $A(w_0
u)=\det(w_0)A(
u)$ for every $
u$, because $\det(ww_0^{-1})=\det(w)\det(w_0)$ and $\det(w_0)^2=1$. The same identity at $
u=ho$ gives $A(-ho)=\det(w_0)A(ho)$. Cancel only the scalar unit $\det(w_0)\in\{1,-1\}$ to obtain $qA(ho)=A(\lambda+ho)$ in $\mathbf Z[X]$, and hence in $\mathbf Q[X]$. Its coefficients are the original rational dimensions by step 1. There has been no localization or cancellation of $A(ho)$.

source.place: 22.50--22.52, printed p.480, with the sign convention from 18c and 22.48 corrected by choosing mu=-w0(lambda).

proof.text: The arguments apply to reducible root systems: they use all roots together and the full Weyl group, with no irreducibility assumption. For the empty root set, the spanning hypothesis forces $X\otimes\mathbf Q=0$, hence $X=0$ since it is free. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], empty roots imply $S=T_F$. The specified split torus has character lattice $0$, so its rank is zero and $S=1$. Every subspace of $V_F$ is then invariant. Simplicity makes the span of any nonzero vector all of $V_F$, so $\dim_F V_F=\dim_{\mathbf Q}V=1$. Thus $\rho=\lambda=0$, $W=\{1\}$, $q=1$ and $A(0)=1$, proving the claimed identity and its finite weight decomposition directly.
